newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA BANKS ON BUY SIDE IN T-BILL MARKET.
newsitem.headline: MANILA BANKS ON BUY SIDE IN T-BILL MARKET.

text.p: Philippine banks started buying treasury bills in the secondary market on Monday ahead of an expected slide in interest rates, traders said.

This view was bolstered when the peso showed relative stability early on Monday when foreign banks started participating again at the foreign exchange spot market after being out of it since the peso's de facto devalutaion on July 11.
"Everyone's starting to buy bills. The market view is that the central bank's overnight borrowing rate could be 15 percent next week from the current 18 percent," one trader said.
In line with this view, banks quoted lower bid and offer rates for T-bills ahead of the auction later today.

Another trader cautioned it might still be too early to tell that interest rates would drop back to normal levels since many restrictions remain in force against foreign banks trading at the spot market.
The average interbank call loan rate was steady at 18.0625 percent. Volume was higher at 18.84 billion pesos from 12.37 billion pesos as banks covered three days of reserve positions.
Out of the 53 participating financial institutions, 31 were lenders.
